A piece up and still not winning? Five simple habits for finishing a won game. ♟️

What's the worst win you ever threw away? 👇

ig_caption:
A piece up, and somehow the game slips away. Finishing a won game is a skill of its own, and it can be learned.

Swap pieces when you are ahead, but keep your pawns: they can become queens later. Keep checking what your opponent's last move threatens, because winning players relax. Watch out for stalemate when they only have a king left: always leave it a square. Once the queens are off, bring your king to the centre. And choose the clean, safe win over the flashy one you can't fully check.

slides.title: A piece up,
slides.sub: FIVE WAYS TO FINISH A WON GAME

slides.title: Swap pieces, keep pawns
slides.body: When you are ahead, each swap of pieces makes your extra piece count for more. Keep your pawns: in the endgame they can become queens.
slides.note: Offer swaps. Don't give away pawns for nothing.

slides.title: Still check their threats
slides.body: Winning players relax and stop looking. Before each move, ask what their last move threatens: a check, a capture, a fork.
slides.note: A comeback often starts with one missed check.

slides.title: Watch out for stalemate
slides.body: If their king is not in check, has no safe square, and they have no other legal move, the game is a draw. It is easy to do with a queen against a lone king.
slides.note: When they only have a king left, always leave it a square, until you give mate.

slides.title: Bring your king in
slides.body: Once the queens are off, your king is a strong piece. Walk it towards the centre to help your pawns and stop theirs.
slides.note: In the endgame, a king left at home is a piece not playing.

slides.title: Pick the safe move
slides.body: You don't need a brilliant finish. If one move wins cleanly and another might win faster but you can't check it all, choose the clean one.
slides.note: Ahead? Ask which move keeps your lead with the least risk.
